product.summary: Back office of a regional freight operator: dispatchers plan routes, follow shipments and resolve exceptions all day.

audience.environment: two monitors, eight-hour shifts, interruptions by phone
laptop in meetings, phone on the warehouse floor

requirements.text: A dispatcher sees what needs attention in the first screen without scrolling: late shipments, unassigned loads, vehicles off plan.
Shifts last eight hours: the interface must stay legible and calm, with no decoration that tires the eye.
Tables hold hundreds of rows; many columns are numbers, identifiers and times that must align and be scannable.
Status (on time, at risk, late, delivered) is the most important signal and must never rely on colour alone.
Managers open the same screens on a phone in the warehouse: the layout reflows to one column and the critical numbers stay first.
Night shifts work in dim rooms: a dark theme is part of the product, not a novelty.
Everything a dispatcher does hourly is reachable with the keyboard; focus is always visible.
Motion only confirms an action or explains a change of state; nothing moves on its own.
The brand is quiet, industrial and trustworthy: a deep blue the company already uses on its trucks, no gradients.

direction.statement:
Quiet and dense. The data is the interface; chrome recedes to thin borders and one accent.
Colour appears only for status and for the single primary action on a screen.
Type is set for scanning: tabular numbers, short labels, generous line height in the rows that matter.
references: the restraint of a well-set annual report
the density of a dispatch board without its colour noise
signage in a freight terminal: large numbers, few words

decisions.choice: One sans family (Inter Variable with system fallbacks) at a 1.2 ratio; tabular numbers everywhere numbers appear; body 16px, table cells 14px with 1.45 line height; no display sizes above 2xl inside the application.

Accent is the fleet blue #1f4e8c used only for the primary action and links; neutrals are a cool grey tinted from the same hue; four status colours (success, warning, danger, info) each paired with an icon and a word.
4px base; rows and controls on 32px and 36px heights (compact density) with 8px and 12px gutters inside cards and 24px between regions.
Compact by default with a comfortable toggle in preferences; the toggle changes row height and padding tokens only.
A 272px sidebar on desktop that collapses to icons at 1024px and to a drawer under 768px; a 12-column page grid with a 1440px maximum; KPI row, then charts, then the exception table.
Soft corners: 4px on controls, 6px on cards, never full rounding except avatars and status dots.
Flat: borders separate regions; a single shadow level for popovers, menus and dialogs, nothing else floats.
120ms for state changes, 200ms for panels and menus, 320ms for the drawer; standard easing; no auto-playing motion; reduced motion cuts.
No decorative imagery; maps and vehicle photos appear only where they carry information; icons from one outline set at 20px.

Hover darkens by one ramp step; focus is a 2px accent ring with 2px offset on every control; disabled lowers opacity to 0.5 and keeps the label readable; selected rows use a tinted surface plus a left border.
Dark theme ships with the product: surfaces step up in lightness as they rise, the accent moves one step lighter for text, status colours keep the same hues.
Targets at least 24px (36px for the primary row actions on touch); every table has a caption and sortable headers announce their state; dialogs trap and restore focus.
Breakpoints by content: 640, 768, 1024, 1280; tables become stacked cards under 768px with the status and identifier first; KPIs stay above the fold on a 375px phone.

states.hover: one ramp step darker (light) or lighter (dark)

imagery.policy: informational only: maps, vehicle photos in detail views; no hero imagery, no illustrations
